reviews.text: Filled to the brim with technical and narrative mastery, David Robert Mitchell’s sophomore feature “It Follows” screams success, both as a horror film and an art form with a voice.
reviews.author: Ankit Ojha

reviews.text: Its meticulous directorial vision and thematic ambition are what make it a modern masterwork. Once you see It Follows it will follow you forever.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Could skirt by on its slick aesthetics alone, but by injecting genuinely frightening sequences and allegorical fears faced by teenagers make for something both fresh and familiar.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: Mitchell’s attention to detail with his writing and directing, coupled with a memorable and orgasmic score from Disasterpiece puts It Follows right up there as... one of the most impactful and unforgettable horrors of all time.
reviews.author: James Perkins

reviews.text: A tonic to the spate of “found footage” and shaky-cam horror films... this is a carefully designed film that recalls the visual control of John Carpenter’s early horror films, especially the way it tracks movement within carefully composed shots.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: There are some truly arresting visuals including some particularly striking uses of perspective. But it’s the story between the images that unfortunately doesn’t hold up.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: One would wonder plot-wise if one of the victims just performed what the Oxford Dictionary describes as “self-abuse,” that could be considered taking one for the team and end the curse entirely.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: "By excluding grown ups from the narrative, 'It Follows' highlights the perseverance of young adults and their reliance on each other for a shared vision."
reviews.author: Q.V. Hough

reviews.text: David Robert Mitchell has made such a superb horror film that its clinging aftereffect continues for an uncommonly long period.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: A hidden gem well worth tracking down for a pre-Halloween shock to the system.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: It may be a silly premise, but Mitchell uses it to the best effect.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Capturing anxiety in a way that no other film has, It Follows is a modern horror masterpiece.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: A methodical, unnerving and surprisingly mean thriller. Mitchell perfectly frames and moves the camera to emphasize how vulnerable his characters are and, in so doing, maximizes the existential dread.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The way it was shot was just flawless.
reviews.author: Emma Wolfe

reviews.text: [It] isn't the first to combine frights with burgeoning teen sexuality, but because his smart script cranks up the tension and without gratuitous gore, this film feels fresh and scary.
reviews.author: Angus Batey

reviews.text: For any fan of this particular genre: this is a must-see. One of the best, stylish, more recent horrors you'll discover. It will creep up on you, and won't let go.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: It's a scary film through and through, but it's the dual horror of teenage boredom and ennui coupled with a strange and terrifying supernatural virus that is transmitted sexually.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A really worthwhile and atmospheric independent horror film.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: The sophistication and patience Mitchell exhibits shows a maturity we desperately need more of. He understands the enjoyment of horror is not just in the climax, but also in the foreplay.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: It Follows is exactly the type of film that the word "chiller" was created to describe. Once you see it, your spine will never be the same.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: The best horror movie of recent years. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: What is unique about 'It Follows' plot-wise is practically null and essentially boils down to the fact that... the triggering action is having sex with someone. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Benítez

reviews.text: 'It Follows' is filled with extraordinary metaphors, all within the film's horror tone and with no lack of scares, that emerge from the most horrifying daily life. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Abuín

reviews.text: I could go on at great length about the dark subtexts swirling underneath It Follows, but the most important thing is that the surface is genuinely terrifying. It's an instant classic.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: So many people are being moved to think and feel things that this movie doesn't actually provide, which is usually a good thing. It just didn't happen for me.
reviews.author: Angela L. Harmon

reviews.text: A persistent film that creeps up on you.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: It Follows is a frightening, original and involving horror movie that totally lives up to the hype.
reviews.author: Joey Keogh

reviews.text: Rather than anything as uninspired as a sex scare movie, It Follows plays more upon the fears and insecurities that plague any teenager, sexually active or not.
reviews.author: Andrew Todd

reviews.text: Whoever It Follows slept with to get the indie horror buzz that's surrounding it, here's hoping their baby-making parts are now the target of demons. It's not good, and you shouldn't see it.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Luckily the creepiness doesn't get drowned out, making It Follows an enjoyable piece of genre fun.
reviews.author: C.J. Prince

reviews.text: It Follows isn't always as subversive as it wants to be, but Mitchell encapsulates teenage sexual paranoia with artfulness and sensitivity, told through the dynamics of Craven-Carpenter horror cinema.
reviews.author: Janz Anton-Iago

reviews.text: A beautifully rendered vision of the teenage psyche in the 21st century, it's a stylish, intelligent and densely textured masterpiece.
reviews.author: Craig Williams

reviews.text: I can't remember the last movie that freaked me out so thoroughly. Great movies stick to the back of your mind; It Follows breathes down the back of your neck.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: Monroe's ability to carry every emotion just under the surface and break down at the exact right moment is INSANE.
reviews.author: Amie Simon

reviews.text: It's such an interesting audience experience...try your hardest not to think about this too much.
reviews.author: May Leitz

reviews.text: Horror fans rejoice, David Robert Mitchell's new film "It Follows" is just for you. The writer/director has taken a simple premise, and a limited budget, and created a genuinely engaging creep show.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It Follows is still good for a few scares, but it's ultimately a little boring because there's nothing interesting between them.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: Please go see this movie. It is the kind of movie that makes you think about it for days afterwards, which means they did a great job.
reviews.author: Molly Henery

reviews.text: Disturbing in its simplicity, It Follows is a multi-layered horror film that is as insidious as it is terrifying.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: A quiet but tremulous vision of teenage physical discomfort and emotional distress.
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: Takes cues from '70s horror movies, but ... creates its own creepy atmosphere.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: An almost entirely successful chiller.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: Mitchell takes the unavoidability of sex as a hotbed of creeping terror, and successfully conjures demons out of the necessary and pleasurable.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: ... It Follows" manages to both take place in a believable world and depart from it in productive ways. Middle America has rarely seemed so scary.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: The film takes sex, a cliché of horror, and uses it to charge a narrative that is smart and compelling and boasts a soundtrack so hypnotic it elevates the intensity on every level.
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: It Follows still impresses as a savvy but sincere exercise in sustained tension-building and release-more of a machine than a film, maybe, but a finely wrought one.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: Yet even though It Follows fails to entirely convince whenever it most closely adheres to genre trappings, the underlying notes of tenderness and sadness are as acutely rendered as they were in [writer/director David Robert] Mitchell's first feature.
reviews.author: Jason Anderson

reviews.text: It's a game I'd be happy to play again.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: It Follows is unnerving without being bloody, and more than this, that it cleverly inverts the sexual politics on which so much popular culture, most especially the horror film, often depends.
reviews.author: Anwen Crawford

reviews.text: It Follows is more than just a terrifying horror movie - it's a heady and heartbreaking exploration of both sexually transmitted disease and sexual abuse, and an unexpectedly poignant riff on the classic coming-of-age narrative.
reviews.author: Scott Meslow

reviews.text: Most horror films tap into a variety of fears, and It Follows is no exception.
reviews.author: Kathy Fennessy

reviews.text: After the striking visuals burnt through the screen, however, the structure underneath was more bark than bite.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: Horror is at its best when it gives you something to think about along with your creeps. The new film It Follows, fits that bill quite well. It also happens to be one of the scariest movies this year.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: It Follows is an incredibly evolved, joyously alive piece of "dead teenager" cinema that likely requires a few viewings to properly assimilate its rhythms.
reviews.author: Chris Alexander

reviews.text: Has no qualm about paralyzing the audience in deafening silence and then unleashing fearful episodes in very gradual doses.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: It Follows is too uneven to fully recommend, but it does contain some of the most disturbing horror imagery. Far from the best horror movie of the year, it is still a vital reminder of how boundary-pushing American genre movies used to be.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: It Follows is classical horror, and deserves to be sculpted into the Mount Rushmore of horror alongside other greats.
reviews.author: Brad Miska

reviews.text: It Follows embodies the dreamlike, sensual hum of a foreign film and a concrete narrative indicative of American cinema.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: It Follows is very much worth investigating, but like so many of its genre it does lose its way slightly at the very end.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: If you've enjoyed The Conjuring and The Babadook then get yourself down to It Follows
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: It Follows is miles and away better than a lot of the low-budget horror that abuses the eyeballs of genre fans, but it's not good enough to be worth the time of people who aren't already into horror (like The Babadook is).
reviews.author: Rebecca Pahle

reviews.text: This impressive throwback to 80s slasher flicks is packing houses for good reason.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: It's a brilliant concept, tapping the same primitive fears -- body horror, burgeoning sexuality -- that underpinned the slasher genre, while reining in the wanton misogyny.
reviews.author: James Hadfield

reviews.text: Last year's brilliant The Babadook set a new bar for horror movies this decade and yet, six months later, that mark has been reached by It Follows.
reviews.author: George Byrne

reviews.text: This is a ghost film whose strength is in the overwhelming air of melancholy. Nothing is scarier, or sadder, than when you have to look back over your shoulder all your life.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: You will leave the cinema looking over your shoulder - and if you see a girl in a yellow dress, just run.
reviews.author: Chris Schulz

reviews.text: The best little horror movie since last year's acclaimed hit The Babadook.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: Little more than a love note to John Carpenter, forgoing invention in favor of full-on homage.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: The genius of It Follows lies in the simplicity of its set-up. ... In Mitchell's intensely creepy movie, the dread only keeps on building until the end.
reviews.author: Edmund Lee

reviews.text: It Follows is a slow and unnerving horror film that builds masterfully; it treats its characters and its audiences intelligently, offering layers beyond the usual horror tropes.
reviews.author: Marija Djurovic

reviews.text: Orchestrating a number of jump scares with surprising grace, the film quotes John Carpenter with its scope lensing, yet also earns the comparison.
reviews.author: Ethan Vestby

reviews.text: It is low-tech stylish, which gives it its convincing power.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: There is something in Mitchell's work that deeply affects us, for he knows how to tap our deepest fear of being left alone and helpless, and push us to face the ultimate dread that we won't know how to deal with it.
reviews.author: Emine Yildirim

reviews.text: It Follows represents a compelling evolution in how studios and audiences can (and should) conceive of its monsters.
reviews.author: Lenika Cruz

reviews.text: The horror of the new century, bet to the subtlety of the faceless monster, but is not less scary. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: Like the best horror films It Follows will stay with you, making you look afresh at those trailing behind. It'll take you back to your own teenage years, reminding you what a terrifying world it can be when the adults step back.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: While the idea might sound slightly ridiculous, Jay and her friends are all so authentic that this stylish flick remains totally believable throughout.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: No question that the storytelling here is impressive; the story itself, however, is a bit thin.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: This is a movie you need to see right now.
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: It's a testament to how scary a movie It Follows is that for days after watching it, you walk around thinking up survival plans - should you hide, stay on the move forever, pass the haunting on to someone else?
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: A good old-fashioned spooky tale that forces us to confront the inevitability of death and asks what we would do if we could see it coming.
reviews.author: Mark H. Harris

reviews.text: With a great handle of fear and paranoia, also with the awesome dark and blue photography, Mitchell creates an atmosphere so tense that you can feel the despair in his characters. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Anaid Ramírez

reviews.text: One of the best horror films in years.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: The photography, sound and feel of the film conjure up a threadbare and tawdry world. Detroit's outer environs are seedy and slumish. It's oddly claustrophobic to its teenage inhabitants, despite being devoid of functioning adults.
reviews.author: Ian Allison

reviews.text: Horror fans might be surprised at the lack of gory action, and yet those willing to let this one work its eerie magic should find that it follows them home.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: It's been a while since a movie made me feel that way, but David Robert Mitchell's It Follows creates that kind of constant anxiety.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Mitchell builds real tension, overwhelming moments of helplessness, and slips of conscience regardless of the time of day. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: It Follows is a rare movie these days, an original horror movie that actually takes itself seriously. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Uma obra que comprova que, nas mãos de um bom diretor, um longa de terror é uma obra de arte tão digna e memorável quanto o mais lacrimoso dos dramas de época.
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Anyone who makes horror films should be inspired by movies like It Follows.
reviews.author: Scott Weinberg

reviews.text: This sort of depth helps make It Follows that rare thing, a horror film that improves on a second viewing.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Monroe is fantastic in the lead, showing us Jay's evolution from skeptic to believer to calculating survivor, and Mitchell has thought his monster through to the last detail.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: It Follows is the real deal.
reviews.author: James Robert Douglas

reviews.text: One of the most provocative horror films in recent history. [Full review in Spanish].
reviews.author: Mario P. Székely

reviews.text: A refined and elegant version of a typical teen horror movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Aguilar

reviews.text: One of the few horror films that does justice to the genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mabel Salinas

reviews.text: One of the best horror films in recent years. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: It builds up great tension between the protagonist and "it," toying with the spectator in a subtle way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: Perfectly captures the theme of teenage angst and the stylized visuals are reminiscent of '80s horror films. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: It's not that scary, but it's beautifully crafted. [Full review in Spanish].
reviews.author: Oswaldo Betancourt Lozano

reviews.text: A great work in atmosphere with solid emotional impact. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Cuauhtémoc Ruelas

reviews.text: The best I've seen of the genre all year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: It Follows is like nothing you've seen in the genre: it's well crafted, beautiful and it's visually stunning. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: An exceptional horror film, one that focuses on innocence lost, and the cruelty of our world...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Not much seems to be going on under the hood.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: A low-octane horror film that gets under your skin and stays there. It's hard to forget "It Follows."
reviews.author: Paul Chambers

reviews.text: The American breakout horror hit has a few things going for it.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: An artful-but-still-terrifying metaphor for the alien world of adulthood, that sense you have as a teen that the world is out to get you, and no one is going to help you.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: The only control the teenagers have in the situation is to pass on the curse - and increase their sexual guilt tenfold. It's a brilliantly clean metaphor, not just for sexual nervousness, but also the transience of youth.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: Ultimately an excellent technical exercise, more interested in sustaining a mood and feeling than exploring the truly scary ideas rattling around beneath the surface of this story.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It Follows is a classy, scary horror show: Pass it on.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Mitchell is much more interested in creating an atmosphere of absolute dread that builds and builds, until your nerves are rattled and shattered. And that uneasy sense of foreboding will linger long after you've exited the theater.
reviews.author: Tim Holland

reviews.text: It Follows is intelligent and terrifying, an instant genre classic.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Like Jennifer Kent's masterful The Babadook, It Follows is anchored by excellent performances and layered with subtext.
reviews.author: AP Kryza

reviews.text: It Follows is without doubt the scariest movie you will see this year. And probably next year, too.
reviews.author: Chris Newbould

reviews.text: ... more concerned with the psychology of horror than the blood and guts, as the film preys on common fears and paranoia without turning manipulative or sacrificing tension.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Earns its place on the list of classic horrors by honouring what came before while staking out bold new ground.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: The film has style, has panache, and a strong vision ... It uses Detroit beautifully, evoking chilling foreboding from rows of deserted houses shot from the car's POV in an autumnal dread.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: In It Follows, sexual activity has metaphysical implications.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The fright film du jour succeeds as both cautionary teen allegory and unnerving blend of 'Blue Velvet' and the underground 'Deadgirl' ... an instant cult classic!
reviews.author: Glenn Lovell

reviews.text: Even on its own kooky, spooky terms there are lapses in plausibility here that even the most forgiving horror fan will spot, but they are more than compensated by the film's sheer number of quality shocks.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Conceived in a way that allows these clichés to be subverted, transforming... safe havens into being more dangerous and terrifying than any of the tropes themselves.
reviews.author: Matt Rice

reviews.text: Last year it was The Babadook, but 2015's must-see horror film is this chic American indie.
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: While I didn't find myself particularly frightened by the film as many have suggested, I marveled at the gorgeous cinematography, retro score, and use of location.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: The performances by the fresh-faced newcomers are spot on.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: That ceaseless slow march will likely become 2015's scariest image.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Ultimately, rather than sex, what seems threatening here is impending adulthood in all its dimensions, and in its floaty, insubstantial way, It Follows catches some of the mingled excitement and terror of growing up.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: It's brilliant.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: It Follows is well worth a look and if you go in not expecting the second coming of horror, you'll likely have a good time with this unique, slowburn supernatural fable.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: The setting is contemporary crumbling Detroit, yet there's a strong '70s and '80s vibe, with some dreamy visuals (above ground swimming pools, cherry red bitten-down fingernails) and a creepy electro synth score by Disasterpeace.
reviews.author: Rochelle Siemienowicz

reviews.text: A kind of art-house horror movie, an allegory about AIDS and, believe it or not, a love story, 'It Follows' is one of a kind.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Mitchell and his cast really make it work, and the soundtrack coats the whole thing in a sort of beautiful dread
reviews.author: Martin Roberts

reviews.text: There's a chance you might, at night, catch yourself looking over your shoulder more than once after watching this.
reviews.author: Reagan Gavin Rasquinha

reviews.text: So this is when I am going to break from the critical chorus of praise. It Follows wasn't flawless for me - and perhaps a victim of its own hype in that regard.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: It Follows is bold, provocative, original, artfully made, perfectly acted, and creepy as hell.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The next time some old lady starts following you with an emotionless stare on her face, you are going to lose your mind.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: It Follows has an impressively sustained sense of dread, less explicit gore than measured tension. Mitchell slyly inverts the conventions of dead-meat teenager flicks, although not with wink-wink comedy like the Scream series.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Formally and visually it is a work of real craftsmanship, and it displays a conscious understanding of the paradoxes of the heart that the horror genre plumbs so well.
reviews.author: Timothy Wainwright

reviews.text: "Follows" Fails to Follow Through
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: It's a wildly fun conceit ... Mitchell's atmospheric rendering of It Follows gives the film a fanciful, otherworldly feel.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Easily the best horror film I've seen since "The Cabin in Woods" (2012), "It Follows" is an instant classic.
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: This is a genuinely creepy movie with a few scary moments, mostly caused by sudden, loud noises and quick film cuts. The landscape of urban decay is used to good effect. The raggedy edges of Detroit look like row upon row of haunted houses.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The perfect viewer for It Follows is one who wants to see the unsettling things that happen when genres and their expectations collide.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Even though the setup creates little more than variations on the same basic threat, the film maintains a rigorous tension that is as unrelenting as the ambiguous monstrosity that keeps coming at us.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Tense, creepy, filled with dread.... We're not afraid of what the characters are afraid of. We're just AFRAID.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: What the movie acknowledges is that the biological imperative that perpetuates the human race carries its own curse of mortality -- that the act of reproduction passes on both the gift of life and a death sentence.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: ...both memorable and controversial, inspiring the kind of water cooler horror-fan talk that the 'The Ring' managed to generate before it was diluted with all the sequels.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Good horror films rely on suspense and tension, and this one has both elements aplenty.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The film might not be as deep as it aspires to be, but It Follows is one retro horror movie that's quite creepy and has style to spare.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: Even when you strip away the subtext and symbolism, It Follows is just a genuinely creepy movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It Follows specifically pays tribute to Carpenter's horror precedent in its middle-class setting, its likable characters and its spare, nerve-fraying musical soundtrack.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: Remember, kids, when you have sex, you're having sex with every person they've ever had sex with. And also with a demon stalking all of you.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The better things in "It Follows" are a tempting tease for what the film's young director will do next.
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: ...unique and arresting.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: "It Follows" is the creepiest movie in years.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: Less a conventional scary horror film than a fitful, disturbing dream, It Follows is all about atmosphere, with an unsettling soundscape and dislocating widescreen imagery.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Despite that title -- and the debt owed to 1970s cinema, most glaringly in the film's creepy techno-organ score -- It Follows largely charts its own path.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: It Follows manages to bend the rules of fateful juvenile sexuality, and does so in a manner that genuinely tingles the spine and disturbs the mind.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: It Follows builds terror that finds its scares through all the earmarks of a very vivid nightmare.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: It's hard not to share Jay's mounting panic as she watches the thing in its various guises walking slowly toward her wherever she may be, invisible to everyone else and entirely intent on destroying her.
reviews.author: Bruce Ingram

reviews.text: It succeeds as a thriller, with performances that strike a grave, quiet tone suited to the film's wide shots, long takes and carefully cultivated mood of foreboding.
reviews.author: Carla Meyer

reviews.text: It horrifies. It disturbs. It rules.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: I wanted to follow it, too.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It Follows has style to burn, and the cinematography, coupled with a nuanced, synth-heavy soundtrack keeps ratcheting up the tension in smart and creative ways.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: The matters of sex and lost innocence work like a thematic undertow, pulling the characters down into the dark, psychological depths.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: Promises more than it delivers, but engrossing throughout.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: It's about many things, but dread infuses them all. You won't be grossed out. You'll be creeped out. And that's a lot more satisfying.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: There's just enough detail to the movie's mythology to make it hold together, and just enough left unexplained to make things genuinely eerie.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: Every once in a while a low-budget indie fright flick comes along that makes everything on the major studios' horror plate look like a pile of steaming crap.
reviews.author: Steve Newton

reviews.text: Accomplished work, always interesting to watch, but it doesn't quite live up to its potential, finding Mitchell scrambling to reclaim suspense lost to budgetary and thespian limitation.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: One of those rare scary machines where everything just clicks together, with a ferociously single-minded rightness that keeps the nerves in a state of high, perpetual thrum.
reviews.author: Andrew Wright

reviews.text: While I don't quite think that David Robert Mitchell's It Follows is one of the scariest movies ever made, it is certainly one of the most unsettling.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: It's all made more powerful and paranoia-inducing because the shuffling stalkers could be anyone, anytime, anywhere. They're as inexplicable as they are impossible to escape.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: Mitchell reshapes tried-and-true scare conventions - teens in peril, a relentless malevolent force, jarring soundtrack - into an unexpectedly unique creepfest. And his riffs on sex and adulthood are refreshing in their allegorical complexity.
reviews.author: Jeff Meyers

reviews.text: Most of it evokes the attacks on lust that flourished in Alfred Hitchcock's Psycho and The Birds and that were rampant in the high school nightmare movies of the 1970s and 1980s.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: Brilliant genre filmmaking, nicely sinister camera moves, excellent cast, superbly terrifying score by Disasterpeace.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It Follows is both scary enough to please horror fans and deep enough to inspire term papers.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: "It Follows" is a truly electrifying, even hair-raising horror film. But it doesn't rely on gore to jangle our nerves. It merely preys on our imagination.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Delivers enough scares for those looking for them. (Full Content Review -- Sex, Profanity, Violence, etc. -- for Parents also available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: It Follows is as scary as it is because, in part, it doesn't try to be scary.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Mitchell's skills in crafting mood and building tension result in one of the most mesmerizing and suspenseful horror movies to come along in a long time.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Follows is an effective pastiche but a studied one; by the end, even its ambiguities feel overdetermined.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: A sophisticated twist on the standard "have sex and die" themes of maniac movies from the late 1970s and early 1980s.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Where most teen horror movies revel in the peer group splintering and getting slaughtered, this one is more interested in how people gather around a loved one and shield her from harm.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Jennifer Kent's The Babadook, from last year, turned parenthood into the scariest story of all, and now comes David Robert Mitchell's It Follows, which merges paranoia and teen sexuality into an exercise in delicious dread.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: An assured piece of filmmaking that works as both a horror movie and a coming-of-age story.
reviews.author: Andrew Welch

reviews.text: Mitchell conjures up plenty of eerie atmospherics - the camerawork and "Halloween"-esque score are excellent - but the film never reaches terrifying heights.
reviews.author: David Lewis

reviews.text: "It Follows" is one of the scariest movies I've ever seen. It's also one of the most beautiful.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Creates a quiet just waiting to be pierced, observing the experience of being young and finding normalcy punctured by something new and potentially scary.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: It Follows deserves to be a hit; it's the pearl you search through loads of home-brewed horror to find.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Michael Gioulakis's cinematography, more art-house than genre with its eerie pools of light at night, brings an arrestingly static, tableau-like quality that echoes the highly staged scenarios of Gregory Crewdson's photos.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: ...David Robert Mitchell's It Follows stands out as one of the stronger horror offerings of recent years.
reviews.author: Kyle Turner

reviews.text: Not since Freddy Krueger stalked teenagers in their sleep have I felt so completely like the poor kids on screen had nowhere to run, and nowhere to hide.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: From the opening moments, the one thing clear about It Follows is that it will not follow in everyone else's footsteps.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: It Follows is itself a film that thrives in the borders, not so much about the horror that leaps out in front of you, but the deeper anxiety that waits at the verge of consciousness.
reviews.author: Dom Sinacola

reviews.text: Written and directed by David Robert Mitchell, It Follows is the latest in a long line of sex-as-horror flicks that somehow grounds its terror both in reality and in the otherworldly, making this a smart and thought-provoking movie.
reviews.author: Hazel Cills

reviews.text: An intricate piece of work that derives its significant scares out of sheer cinematic bravado.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: It's an undeniable triumph of mood - perfect for anyone who wants to practice clenching their fists for nearly 100 straight minutes - as well as an ambitious effort at reinventing horror by eschewing the genre's common tricks.
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: Mitchell pulls off a tricky balance with his ingenious response to 80's horror films where teenage sex meant death and monsters walked leafy suburban streets in broad daylight by presenting his original, nightmarish idea via an homage to John Carpenter.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: "It Follows" is not really about sex, but an unbearable, unsinkable mood that descends when you come of age, and never completely dissipates, not even after climactic sexual, or other violent acts.
reviews.author: Simon Abrams

reviews.text: Unlike many working in this genre, Mitchell doesn't punish young women for having sex: This is a gender-blind demonic delivery vehicle.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: My whole life I've been a horror-movie freak, and I've rarely been as scared as I was at It Follows. But it wasn't a fun kind of scare. It was the so-upset-I-feel-sick kind of amorphous dread.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: A creepy, counterintuitive fright fest that puts a perverse spin on the meaning of getting lucky.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: "It Follows" pretty much earns its buzz as the scariest and best-engineered American horror movie of recent years, and that's all down to Mitchell's sophisticated understanding of technique and the trust and freedom he accords his youthful cast.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: One more stylish reminder of how readily we the people can be creeped out.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: [A] smart, relentlessly chilling thriller that opts for originality over cheaply rejiggered jolts.
reviews.author: Michael Rechtshaffen

reviews.text: A dizzyingly tense and creepy workout.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: Can one perfectly-executed shot redeem the less successful earlier attempts? In this case, after the initial awe wears off, the effect is the opposite: it only makes you realize how much more there was to mine from Mitchell's premise all along.
reviews.author: Tomas Hachard

reviews.text: It Follows is yet another example of how smart the indie horror game is these days.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Rather than breaking new ground, "It Follows" recycles familiar teenage horror tropes - a girl alone in a house, evil forces banging on a door - but its mood is dreamy. Seldom do you feel manipulated by exploitative formulas.
reviews.author: Stephen Holden

reviews.text: Agreeably unsettling if not the terrifying experience some have claimed.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: [A] teen slasher with one killer hook
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: There are ordinary homages and then there are high-quality cinematic mix tapes like It Follows.
reviews.author: Ethan Alter

reviews.text: It Follows may have a pretty terrifying premise - the kind of story that urban legends are born from - but it's much scarier in concept than execution.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: The creature's terrifying persistence taps into a base fear that audiences may not have felt this strongly since Romero's slow-moving living dead first shambled onto screen.
reviews.author: Austin Trunick

reviews.text: Writer-director David Robert Mitchell has clearly studied up on John Carpenter. But Mitchell has his own twisted gift for letting atmosphere help define character. It Follows creeps you out big-time.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The film turns its viewers into paranoid spectators, scanning the frame for signs of trouble.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: With long-building fears and sudden shocks both in profusion, It Follows is one of the better horror films in recent memory precisely because it turns the border between the everyday and the supernatural into a knife-edge that cuts deep into your fears.
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: In love with old-school John Carpenter scares, this film will unsettle you from its first moments. Some of its ideas are just as chilling as its shocks.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: The most fun will be in dissecting it afterwards. Film school professors, look forward to a decade of term papers.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: A radically fresh, hair-raisingly inventive take on a thought-worn subgenre. In spite of its stop-and-start narrative structure, few motion pictures achieve the level of usurping dread that "It Follows" manages.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: Mitchell puts a twist on familiar tropes, enhanced by Rich Vreeland's eerily atmospheric electronic score and witty references to horror-meisters from George A. Romero to John Carpenter.
reviews.author: Michael D. Reid

reviews.text: If the kids think this is the scariest thing ever, then so be it.
reviews.author: Chuck Wilson

reviews.text: Mitchell's deft handling of relationships gets threaded into an ingenious and exceedingly skillful creepshow.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: A relentless working of the nerves done with techniques cribbed from the avant-garde.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: "It Follows" is a fine title, blending a logician's briskness with the job description of a stalker, and David Robert Mitchell, the writer and director, has fun with his various predators.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Though visionary, David Robert Mitchell's film abounds in undigested ideas and dubious sexual politics.
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: Part 2 will surely establish the monster has a twitter account.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: As kind to its audience as it is to its characters.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: The crash-bang-wallop set pieces are economically choreographed and efficiently edited, but their real weight comes from the sense of brooding menace established in interim sequences in which not very much appears to be happening.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: This is horror boiled down to its bones.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: The remorseless antagonist is genuinely horrifying, all the more so because its malignity is seemingly motiveless.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Mitchell is sensitive to the complicated nuances of teenage friendship, rooting the horror in relationships that are believable and affecting.
reviews.author: Kim Newman

reviews.text: This brilliantly unsettling, determinedly awkward film confirms that there is plenty of life in the high-end horror movie.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Wait. Really? Horror movies are still doing the punishing-girls-for-having-sex thing? Ah, but this is 80s retro, so it's 'okay,' then.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Acted on me as all good horror films should, generating that prickly shiver through the shoulders and into the neck.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Mitchell's skill is to take this prosaic truism and turn it into poetry that is as terrifying and seductive as the score (by Disasterpeace), which ranges from the plaintively melancholy to crunchy, distorted walls of electronic noise.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: The ingenious new teen horror film It Follows will intrigue, puzzle and trouble audiences by turns.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The first thing that strikes you about It Follows is that it's a film made with love. And that's something that you infrequently get to say about horror films.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: You won't see anything more scary this year. Unless it sees you first.
reviews.author: Rob Daniel

reviews.text: Just when it seemed that there would never be another original teen horror movie comes this rough-edged but pleasingly creepy American indie ...
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: It Follows unremittingly pursues the two greatest themes in both art and life, as its adolescent kids learn to stave off with sex, however temporarily, the ineluctable approach of death.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: I don't think I have ever had a nightmare quite as scary as this film - a modern classic of fear to be compared to something by a young Carpenter or De Palma.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: With an inventive retro style, writer-director David Robert Mitchell offers an enjoyable riff on the teen horror movie...
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It won't let you go and you can't shake it off. Whether you like it or not.
reviews.author: Ben Rawson-Jones

reviews.text: A horror film that will haunt your waking hours for weeks. Every frame of It Follows is stamped with nameless dread.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: Passive and relentless, familiar and terrifying, predictable and shocking - and impossible to shake off.
reviews.author: Tom Huddleston

reviews.text: A sense of dread envelopes every scene thanks to combination of Mitchell's slow, measured tracking shots and the stunning score from Disasterpeace.
reviews.author: David Edwards

reviews.text: A bold, terrifying attack of cinema, immersive on the levels of imagery both beautiful and grotesque, and scares from the shallowest to the most pervasive.
reviews.author: Ian Mantgani

reviews.text: Mitchell's measured camera movements and dedication to slow burn scares with big, terrifying payoffs are worth the price of admission alone.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Go into It Follows oblivious of what you're about to see and you'll exit terrified. It lingers.
reviews.author: Justin Gerber

reviews.text: It Follows is a lot like sex; even when it's kind of bad it's still pretty good.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: There's a primal fear at work here - everyone gets nervous about being followed - and even though the monster is fiction, I suspect the anxiety may pursue the viewer home.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Suspenseful, atmospheric and spine-tingling horror cinema which nods at the masters and completely astounds as it manages the tough feat of being striking, sensitive and utterly disturbing.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: A low budget horror that injects new blood into the genre's evergreen 'teen sex has horrifying consequences' trope.
reviews.author: Ian Gilchrist

reviews.text: It's not about why things happen so much as it's about why those things can be frightening.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: A lot of horror movies use sex, or talk about sex, or even talk about how other horror movies use sex, but very few get to the root of what's actually scary about it.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: ...one of the most inventive, exciting, and truly frightening horror flicks to come around in ages.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Despite all the fun-to-unpack ideas swirling around Mitchell's premise, this is first and foremost a showcase for his considerable talents as a widescreen visual stylist ...
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: David Robert Mitchell's idea might be the definition of "Slow Burn", but besides a few insignificant pacing issues, It Follows is a horrific work of art with a fresh, rewarding concept.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Truly unsettling. One of the best horror movies to come along in a while.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Starting off strong before losing its way in the end, this stylish, suspenseful chiller should significantly broaden Mitchell's audience without disappointing his early supporters in the slightest.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Refreshingly unironic in its retro vibe (it nods to the classics, but never winks), for us It Follows worked like gangbusters as an exercise in atmosphere and allusion...
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: Canny manipulation of tone, atmosphere and tension makes this a satisfying little horror movie.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Tender, remarkably ingenious and scalp-pricklingly scary.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Plays the teen horror conventions skillfully - and attractively ...
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: It's a work that manages to be both old school and very fresh, a wonderfully restrained film that still packs quite a punch.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

synopsis: After carefree teenager Jay (Maika Monroe) sleeps with her new boyfriend, Hugh (Jake Weary), for the first time, she learns that she is the latest recipient of a fatal curse that is passed from victim to victim via sexual intercourse. Death, Jay learns, will creep inexorably toward her as either a friend or a stranger. Jay's friends don't believe her seemingly paranoid ravings, until they too begin to see the phantom assassins and band together to help her flee or defend herself.
